assumptions_invoked: Arrangement fee paid at t=0 treated as a payment
24 equal monthly repayments starting one month after drawdown
weakest_point: Rounding of monthly payment to euros; no exact payment amount given, so we assumed 450 exactly. The APRC is sensitive to the exact timing of the fee payment (t=0 assumed).

assumptions_invoked: Overdraft assumption per Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part II point (d): full amount drawn immediately, duration assumed 3 months
Interest at 12% nominal per annum charged monthly on outstanding balance
Monthly account fee paid at end of each month
Repayment of principal at end of 3 months
weakest_point: Interest is assumed to be paid monthly (as it is charged), but the directive’s assumption for APRC might treat all interest as paid at the end if not specified. Also, the duration assumption (3 months) is a default that may not match actual practice.

assumptions_invoked: Open-end credit assumption per Annex I Part II point (e): credit provided for 1 year; repaid in 12 equal monthly instalments
Interest at 18% nominal per annum monthly compounding
Monthly payment computed using the nominal rate to amortize the principal
weakest_point: The monthly payment is rounded to 2 decimals; any rounding affects the APRC slightly. Also, the assumption of 12 equal monthly instalments is a default; if the agreement specified a different schedule, the APRC would differ.

assumptions_invoked: Unascertainable drawdown: per Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part II point (c), assume full amount drawn immediately
8% nominal interest on the total drawdown
Broker fee of €200 is financed into the balance, so drawdown = 5000 + 200 = 5200
weakest_point: The key distinction: a financed fee is included in the drawdown and does not appear as a separate payment at t=0, unlike a cash fee which would reduce the net proceeds and increase the APR. Here, the APRC equals the nominal rate because the fee is fully financed and the only cost is interest on the total amount.
